stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Jonathan Stein of Douglas Elliman
stories.excerpt: For Jonathan Stein, the best is yet to come. Stein, 43, joined the real estate game in 2015 after spending time in the private equity space and then going on the road with his best friend’s rock band, Phantogram, as the tour manager. Now, he runs the Jonathan Stein Team at Douglas Elliman. Stein oversees a group of eight brokers at the firm, which has worked on deals ranging from $1 million to over $15 million. When former New York Mets and current Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler needed to sell his SoHo penthouse at 73 Wooster Street, Stein and team member Gavin Shiminski stepped in, helping the major leaguer sell the unit for $26 million. It was one of the five largest sales in New York City in July. The road to such a successful real estate career wasn’t easy, but Stein said real estate is an amalgamation of his favorite things: design, architecture, mixing different personalities, and working well with people. “I got into real estate the old fashioned way — my life blew up and I needed a new career,” he said. “I was waiting tables at a buddy’s restaurant looking for what was going to come next. A friend suggested real estate and I loved the idea.” Commercial Observer caught up with Stein in August for “Get to Know the Broker,” a series where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career? Jonathan Stein: I haven’t done it yet. Check back next year. What is your career Everest? Doing my own development project! What’s something you think people would be surprised to learn about you? I grew up on a farm in a town of 170 people. We raised cattle and pigs, and I showed pigs in 4-H as a kid to help earn money for college. What’s your go-to takeout order? Sushi from my neighborhood omakase spot. What TV show are you currently binging? “All Creatures Great and Small.” What is your silliest pet peeve? When
bullets: Jonathan Stein team, Douglas Elliman, closed $26M SoHo penthouse sale
Broker brokerage deals range $1M–$15M+ across New York City
High-touch relationship-building and design expertise drive luxury residential brokerage
stories.summary: Douglas Elliman broker Jonathan Stein and team closed a $26 million penthouse sale at 73 Wooster Street in SoHo for MLB pitcher Zack Wheeler, one of NYC's five largest residential sales in July. Stein's eight-person brokerage focuses on high-end residential deals ranging from $1 million to over $15 million. The article emphasizes relationship-building and cross-functional expertise (design, architecture, personality management) as drivers of success in luxury residential brokerage.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is a luxury condo/individual property brokerage profile. However, broker networks and deal flow in high-barrier-to-entry markets like Manhattan signal tight supply and strong pricing power for residential product, which can inform competitive positioning and pricing strategy for luxury multifamily in gateway markets.

stories.title: Rejection and Change Are Constants in Residential Brokerage. Adapt.
stories.excerpt: When I decided to get my real estate license, it’s safe to say I had no idea what I was in for. The perception of real estate agents is not the reality. A lot of people assume it’s about the money, but, for me, it’s really all about building and nurturing relationships. I’ve closed many deals by focusing on what was best for my clients, even when it required extra flexibility and problem-solving on my end. I realized early on that half the battle was just being available and accessible, and that building trust and transparency from the first call is key. As a young agent in the industry, I didn’t come into real estate with many connections. Most of my circle wasn’t ready to purchase a home or hire an agent for a rental. I had to find my own path, generating leads organically. But, as a young agent, I was extremely motivated to do so, and I was ready to adapt if needed. Mackenzie Kyle. PHOTO: Courtesy Platinum Properties One of my first deals was in the Financial District. My client’s mom found my profile on RentHop and called me out of the blue. We spoke about her search, and she asked if I could show an apartment in an hour. I lived an hour away from the building at this time, so I quickly rushed over. After a day of last-minute tours, I helped them find an apartment they loved. Their daughter was fresh out of school, and they were nervous about her moving to New York City, but, with my guidance and reassurance, they felt confident that the apartment was the right choice. I didn’t know this deal would jump-start my entire career, but it did. Not only do I still have an amazing relationship with these clients and have helped them find multiple homes, I was also connected with so many amazing referral clients from them because of the superior level of service that I provided. bullets: Young residential broker built practice via organic lead generation and RentHop
Client accessibility, trust, transparency, and problem-solving drive deal velocity
Flexibility and adaptability essential to overcome limited initial industry connections
stories.summary: A young residential broker describes the unglamorous reality of brokerage success: organic lead generation, extreme availability, transparency, and willingness to adapt. Early deals came from unexpected sources (a client's mother finding the broker on RentHop). The broker emphasizes that relationship trust and hands-on service matter more than capital or pre-existing network, and that rejection and change are constants requiring continuous adaptation.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. This is a residential brokerage career narrative without market, supply, demand, or capital signals.

stories.title: The Broker’s Guide to Winning Certainty in Bridge Lending

The firm underwrites loans from $200,000 to $7 million (larger deals case-by-case) on multifamily, mixed-use, condo, co-op, and single-family rental properties. Key differentiators are same-day term sheets on complete, eligible submissions and funding in as few as seven days.
stories.impact: Signals healthy bridge debt competition and speed in the residential/multifamily market, reducing execution risk for acquisitions and value-add deals. Rapid certainty on non-permanent financing is critical for developers in competitive bid situations; this advertisement suggests lender capacity and appetite remain available even in a challenging capital environment, though no new market-specific deal flow is revealed.

stories.title: Podcast: Using AI to Make Better CRE Acquisition & Underwriting Decisions
stories.excerpt: Steven Song is the founder and CEO of Diald, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform for commercial real estate. Before founding Diald, Steven worked on both the investing and development sides of real estate, and built his career across architecture and urban planning, training at Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania. He was a founding principal at SCAAA, a global strategy, planning, and design firm, and is a partner at Axle Companies, a family office focused on real estate investment and social impact ventures. Steven is based in Los Angeles. stories.summary: Steven Song, founder and CEO of Diald, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform for commercial real estate, appeared on a podcast discussing how AI can improve CRE acquisition and underwriting decisions. Song has worked on both investment and development sides, with training in architecture and urban planning (Carnegie Mellon, UPenn) and prior roles as founding principal at SCAAA and partner at Axle Companies (family office focused on real estate). The podcast covers topics including judgment-driven CRE decisions, contextual drift risk, AI token costs, and where human judgment still prevails.
stories.impact: Emerging AI tooling for underwriting may accelerate deal evaluation cycles and reduce analyst overhead, potentially compressing deal timelines and lowering cost of capital deployment for multifamily developers. However, no market signal, capital availability, or supply-demand data is present; this is primarily a vendor/thought-leadership story.

stories.title: Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M
stories.excerpt: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York City-based real estate investment platform focused on opportunistic, distressed and special situations across the U.S., reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II, the firm’s second flagship investment vehicle. Fund II reached its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments and has raised an additional $120 million in co-investments to date. Fund II received support from a diverse group of new and returning institutional investors, including public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and private investors. Fund II exceeded Machine’s debut fund, Machine Real Estate Fund I, which closed in 2022 with $246 million in primary commitments and $208 million in co-investments. “We are humbled by the support of our investment partners, including both returning Fund I investors and a number of new institutional relationships, which allowed us to reach our hard cap for Fund II,” said Eric Rosenthal, co-founder and managing partner of Machine Investment Group. “Reaching our hard cap in what continues to be a challenging fundraising environment, particularly for middle market managers pursuing a diversified strategy, is a milestone we do not take for granted.” Representative Fund II investments include a special situations powered land investment in Pennsylvania, a distressed 539-unit residential property in downtown San Jose, a 229-unit senior housing property on Long Island acquired out of a distressed situation, a recently developed 1.3 million square foot industrial park in Phoenix and a strategic capital investment in a publicly traded company being repositioned as a powered land and data center development platform. The post Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Machine Investment Group Fund II closed at $350M hard cap + $120M co-investment
Fund II exceeded Fund I ($246M primary + $208M co-invest, closed 2022)
NYC-based platform targeting opportunistic, distressed, special situations nationally
stories.summary: Machine Investment Group, a New York City-based opportunistic and distressed real estate investment platform, reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II at a hard cap of $350 million in primary commitments plus an additional $120 million in co-investments. Fund II exceeds the firm's debut fund (2022), which closed with $246 million primary and $208 million co-investments. Institutional backers include public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices, and private investors. Co-founder Eric Rosenthal cited the closed-end raise as a milestone in a challenging fundraising environment, especially for middle-market diversified platforms.
stories.impact: Indicates that institutional capital is still allocating to distressed and opportunistic strategies despite a tough fundraising environment. For multifamily developers, this signals lingering opportunity in off-market or complex deals (e.g., stabilization, repositioning, forced sales) where institutional capital is prepared to partner or acquire. Growth from Fund I to Fund II suggests appetite for scaled, diversified middle-market platforms—relevant for developers considering institutional JVs or partnerships on value-add transactions.

stories.title: Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Kennedy Wilson said Wednesday that Jaime Lee has joined the firm as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. Most recently CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison, Lee joins Kennedy Wilson as the firm continues to expand its investment management platform and deepen relationships with institutional and private capital partners.   In her new role, Lee will help lead capital formation initiatives, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and help drive investment opportunities across Kennedy Wilson’s global real estate platform.  “Jaime brings an exceptional combination of investment expertise, operational experience and longstanding relationships across both the private and public sectors,” said William McMorrow, chairman and CEO of Kennedy Wilson. “As we continue to grow our investment management platform and expand our capital formation capabilities, Jaime’s proven ability to build partnerships, identify opportunities and navigate complex transactions will be invaluable.” Lee joins Kennedy Wilson following more than 20 years at Jamison, where she helped transform the company into one of Southern California’s largest privately held real estate owners and developers.  The post Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Jaime Lee, former Jamison CEO, joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
Lee brings 20+ years development/investment ops experience, relationships across sectors
Role focuses capital formation, investor relations, deal sourcing across Kennedy Wilson platforms
stories.summary: Kennedy Wilson hired Jaime Lee, former CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison (a multifamily/real estate operator), as Senior Managing Director of Capital Markets and Real Estate Investments. Lee spent over 20 years at Jamison, where she helped build the company into a major operator. Her new role emphasizes capital formation, institutional investor relations, and deal identification across Kennedy Wilson's global real estate platform. Kennedy Wilson CEO William McMorrow highlighted Lee's partnership-building, opportunity identification, and complex-transaction navigation skills.
stories.impact: Signals Kennedy Wilson's commitment to scaling its investment management and capital-raising platform, particularly around multifamily and development. Lee's operational and investor-relations background suggests Kennedy Wilson is positioning to compete for large institutional mandates and co-investment opportunities. For competitors and partners, this hire indicates Kennedy Wilson will likely increase acquisition velocity and capital deployment in multifamily, potentially increasing competition for deal flow in core markets.

stories.title: Developer Iadisernia Lands Mezz Loan to Finish Hallandale, Fla., Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: More than a year after landing a $112 million loan to complete a mixed-use project in Hallandale Beach, Fla., developer Giuseppe Iadisernia has secured yet more debt. Cottonwood Group supplied a $50 million mezzanine loan for a 250-unit condo tower within the 10-acre Oasis mixed-use development at 1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard, about a mile west of the beach, the L.A.-based lender announced Wednesday. Construction is expected to be completed next year. Emile Schachter’s WD Capital Group brokered the debt. A representative for the lender has yet to provide figures regarding condo sales. Last year, S3 Capital had provided the $112 million construction loan for the 25-story tower, considered the last phase of the mixed-use broader development. Prices range from $580,000 and $3.5 million. Just last month, the first condo tower, also a 250-unit, 25-story high-rise, secured a temporary certificate of occupancy up to the 12th floor. The development includes a commercial portion with about 35,000 square feet of office space and 60,000 square feet of retail space, which was completed in 2024. Since the pandemic, when northerners flocked to Florida, Hallandale has been going upscale. In 2024, Witkoff and PPG Development nabbed a $273 million construction loan for a 20-story condo and hotel building within their exclusive Shell Bay golf country club. But some projects have struggled. In March, Monroe Capital sued PPG Development’s Ari Pearl and the principals of BH3 over a $70 million loan tied to Hallandale Beach Residences, The Real Deal reported. The lender alleged the developer stopped making payments in February. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Cottonwood Group provided $50M mezz loan on 250-unit condo tower, Hallandale Beach, Fla.
Oasis mixed-use project includes 10 acres; condo prices $580K–$3.5M; completion expected 2025
Prior construction loan: $112M (S3 Capital, 2023); first phase achieved partial TCO
stories.summary: Developer Giuseppe Iadisernia secured a $50 million mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group for a 250-unit luxury condo tower at the Oasis mixed-use development (1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard, Hallandale Beach, Florida). The 10-acre project is in its final phase; the condo tower, a 25-story high-rise, is expected to complete construction in 2025 with unit prices ranging from $580,000 to $3.5 million. An earlier $112 million construction loan from S3 Capital funded the project; the first 250-unit phase recently secured a temporary certificate of occupancy to the 12th floor.
stories.impact: Mezz financing availability on nearly-completed residential projects signals lender appetite for South Florida residential and willingness to layer debt structures. However, the timing and size ($50M for a 250-unit tower near completion) suggests prior financing gaps and possible demand/sales challenges, requiring additional capital injection. For developers in South Florida, this signals that mezz debt remains available for value-add/completion scenarios, but conventional debt capacity may remain tighter than pre-2022; watch Oasis pre-sales absorption and pricing trends as a bellwether for luxury condo demand in Hallandale Beach/South Florida market.

stories.title: Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster
stories.excerpt: MCB Real Estate, an institutional commercial real estate investment management firm and developer with nationwide holdings, and Osiris Ventures, an urban retail-focused investment firm, have secured leases with two major retail brands at Century Marketplace, the $130-million mixed-use redevelopment of the 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage at 458 86th St. in Brooklyn’s Bay Ridge neighborhood. A national grocery anchor has signed a lease at the property, becoming the first national grocer to serve the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area. National designer-discount retailer Burlington has also signed on, and together the two leases total 60,112 square feet. With these additions, the 120,000-square-foot Century Marketplace is now 65% pre-leased. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” said MCB principal Drew Gorman. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known commercial corridor and unlocking long term value for Southwest Brooklyn.” The post Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Century Marketplace (14-lot, $130M redevelopment) now 65% pre-leased, 120K sq ft retail
National grocer + Burlington signed leases totaling 60,112 sq ft (first national grocer in SW Brooklyn trade area)
MCB Real Estate + Osiris Ventures executing complex mixed-use retail repositioning, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn
stories.summary: MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures have leased 60,112 square feet at Century Marketplace, a $130 million redevelopment of the former Century 21 department store assembly (14-lot site at 458 86th Street, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn). A national grocery chain and Burlington (national discount retailer) signed leases; the grocer is the first national grocer to serve the Southwest Brooklyn trade area. The 120,000-square-foot mixed-use project is now 65% pre-leased.
stories.impact: Demonstrates successful repositioning of obsolete anchor retail into mixed-use with national grocery and discount retail anchors. For multifamily developers, this signals opportunity in adjacent/complementary residential development in revitalized retail corridors (e.g., Bay Ridge), where new grocery and retail infrastructure supports walkability and resident convenience. The grocery anchor's entry into an underserved trade area suggests demand-driven neighborhood upgrading and could justify new multifamily product in the immediate submarket; grocery and retail anchors are leading indicators of neighborhood-level investment and rental demand.

stories.title: Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price
stories.excerpt: Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap arranged the $13.7-million sale of 2515 E. Coast Highway, a prominent multi-tenant retail property located in Corona del Mar. The transaction was represented by Nathan Holthouser of Coastal Commercial and Ron Duong of Marcus & Millichap. The offering generated significant interest from the Orange County investment community, attracting more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding. Prospective buyers consisted primarily of high-net-worth private investors with ties to Orange County. Ultimately, the property sold for $700,000 above its asking price. “The response to this offering was exceptional, but I think sophisticated investors quickly recognized the underlying value of the real estate,” said Holthouser. “You have incredible frontage along Pacific Coast Highway, approximately 20 onsite parking spaces — which is extremely difficult to replicate in Corona del Mar — and a collection of mostly smaller commercial spaces that lend themselves well to maximizing rents over time.” The post Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multi-tenant retail at 2515 E. Coast Hwy., Corona del Mar, sold for $13.7M (above asking)
Property attracted 10+ offers; sold $700K above ask; significant local buyer interest
Parking (20 spaces), oceanfront/highway frontage, and small commercial spaces high-value attributes
stories.summary: A multi-tenant retail property at 2515 E. Coast Highway in Corona del Mar sold for $13.7 million, $700,000 above the asking price. Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale, which generated more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding from high-net-worth local investors. Key attributes cited were oceanfront/highway frontage, approximately 20 onsite parking spaces (rare in Corona del Mar), and multiple smaller commercial spaces allowing rent upside.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the competitive bidding and above-ask sale in Orange County signal strong demand for coastal retail real estate with unique attributes (parking, frontage). For multifamily developers, this underscores the scarcity value and pricing power of rare assets in supply-constrained coastal markets; parking and lifestyle amenities drive investment demand. May inform mixed-use development strategy in Orange County coastal submarkets.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Financing for Stamford Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $74.5-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of The Caspian, a luxury development in Stamford, CT. The Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team led by Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Dustin Stolly, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the financing, provided by an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, on behalf of Sun Homes and Hudson Bay Capital. Located at 68-70 Seaview Ave., the project will transform an existing seven-story, 241,000-square-foot waterfront office building into 63 luxury condominium residences featuring a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom homes along with townhome residences. Amenities include a grand lobby, indoor and outdoor amenity spaces, private rooftop terraces, a 57-slip marina and structured parking. “Fairfield and Westchester counties remain highly supply-constrained residential markets, particularly for new waterfront product given limited developable shoreline and complex entitlement processes,” said Jonathan Schwartz. “The Caspian is uniquely positioned to address that supply-demand imbalance with a best-in-class luxury offering in one of the region’s most desirable waterfront locations. We’re grateful to Sun Homes, Hudson Bay Capital, and Apollo Global Management for their partnership in bringing this vision forward.” The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges Financing for Stamford Residential Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranged $74.5M loan (Apollo affiliate) for Stamford residential conversion
The Caspian converts 241K sq ft, 7-story office tower into 63 luxury condos + marina
Fairfield/Westchester counties supply-constrained; waterfront supply extremely limited; 2025 completion expected
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $74.5 million loan provided by an Apollo Global Management affiliate for Sun Homes and Hudson Bay Capital to acquire and redevelop The Caspian, a waterfront office-to-residential conversion in Stamford, Connecticut. The project converts a 241,000-square-foot, seven-story office building at 68-70 Seaview Avenue into 63 luxury condos (mix of one-, two-, three-bedroom units and townhomes) with amenities including grand lobby, rooftop terraces, a 57-slip marina, and parking. Walker & Dunlop noted that Fairfield and Westchester counties are highly supply-constrained for new residential, particularly waterfront product.
stories.impact: Strong signal of institutional capital appetite for office-to-residential conversion in supply-constrained coastal markets near NYC. Stamford's waterfront location, limited developable shoreline, and complex entitlements create natural scarcity, supporting conversion economics. For multifamily developers in Fairfield/Westchester/lower Fairfield County submarkets, this confirms robust demand for luxury residential and validates conversion/repositioning strategies as alternative to ground-up development. The $74.5M loan size on a 63-unit luxury project (~$1.18M per unit) reflects strong underwriting confidence; watch Stamford/Fairfield County for similar office conversion opportunities and expect competitive bidding for waterfront/coastal office assets.
